answer: Graduated capability limits resist Sybil attacks: a new identity starts with a tiny transaction cap, like one pearl buried in a dune of sand, and only earns higher limits through months of successful, peer-attested work. An attacker who spawns a thousand fakes gets a thousand capped accounts, each too weak to move a market or flood the network. Raising a fake cap takes the same slow history a real agent builds, and the onyx-hard rule is that caps never transfer between identities, so buying an old account cannot shortcut the climb. The cost per useful fake is months of honest work.
